To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified and characterized a novel copy number variant in the Nfκb1 gene, that this CNV is associated with differential susceptibility of A vs B6 mice to CRC, and that this CNV affects the expression of NfκB, which is a key regulator of the inflammatory response in the colon.

we have mapped a locus that regulates differential susceptibility of mice to chemically induced colorectal cancer (A/J, susceptible, C57BL/ 6J, resistant) and have identified a candidate gene that may be responsible.
we have identified a unique 54 bp copy number variant (duplication) in the Nfκb1 gene, which is associated with resistance to colorectal carcinogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of genes that regulate the susceptibility of mouse strains to carcinogen-induced CRC, a model of human CRC, and with the identification of the genes that underlie the differential susceptibility.
the molecular basis of differential susceptibility to CRC in mouse models and the potential role of Nfkb1 and Slc39a in this process.
the molecular characterization of the Ccs1 and Ccs3 CRC loci, and their potential use as models for human CRC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ccs3 locus is likely to contain more than one gene.
the Ccs3 gene has not been identified, but the Nfκβ1 gene is a positional candidate gene that merits further study.
the Ccs3 gene is likely to be the Nfkb gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Nfκb1 gene is the most promising candidate for the Ccs3 locus, and that the Nfkb pathway is likely to play an important role in CRC.
the Ccs3 locus is a complex locus that contains multiple genes, and that NfκB1 and Slc39a7 are likely to play a role in regulating susceptibility to CRC.
we have identified two candidate genes, one with a CNV and one with differential expression, and that both are differentially expressed in CRC tumors from the susceptible A strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CNVs in non-coding regions are likely to be important contributors to complex phenotypes.
the Ccs3 CRC susceptibility locus is complex, and that it contains multiple candidate genes.
a CNV in a noncoding region of NfκB1 may be responsible for the Ccs3 locus effect on CRC susceptibility in the mouse.
